title: A Sparsity Analysis of Traffic Forecasting Architectures: How Much Missing Data is Too Much?
abstract: arXiv:2611.26847v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Traffic forecasting models are typically evaluated under ideal conditions with complete data. This evaluation does not reflect the frequent sensor failures and communication outages common in real-world deployments. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of multivariate traffic prediction models to evaluate their performance under varying levels of sensor data loss during inference. We benchmark several architectural paradigms, including graph neural networks, attention-based Transformers, and selective state-space models, across sparsity levels ranging from zero to complete sensor loss, using two widely used multi-channel traffic benchmarks. To ensure consistent comparison across traffic variables, we use normalized metrics and define a usability threshold to identify when predictions become unreliable. translated_title: 交通预测架构的稀疏性分析：多少缺失数据才算过多？
translated_abstract: 交通预测模型通常在数据完整的理想条件下进行评估，这种评估方式未能反映现实部署中频繁出现的传感器故障和通信中断。本文对多变量交通预测模型进行了全面分析，评估其在推理过程中面对不同程度传感器数据缺失时的性能表现。我们在从零缺失到完全传感器丢失的稀疏度范围内，使用两个广泛使用的多通道交通基准数据集，对包括图神经网络、基于注意力的Transformer以及选择性状态空间模型在内的多种架构范式进行了基准测试。为确保各交通变量之间的比较一致性，我们采用归一化指标，并定义了一个可用性阈值，用于识别预测何时变得不可靠。我们的结果显示出基准精度与鲁棒性之间存在明显的权衡：在全数据条件下精度最高的模型……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文系统评估了图神经网络、Transformer和选择性状态空间模型等交通预测架构在从零到完全传感器缺失的不同稀疏度下的表现，揭示了基准精度与缺失数据鲁棒性之间的权衡，并定义了预测可靠性阈值。
en_tdlr: This paper benchmarks traffic forecasting architectures (GNNs, Transformers, and selective state-space models) across sparsity levels from zero to complete sensor loss, revealing a clear trade-off between baseline accuracy and robustness to missing data, and defining a usability threshold for prediction reliability.
